name: ReceiptKit for WooCommerce
author: receiptkit

sections.description:
Print real receipts for your online orders — not invoices, receipts. Two ways to print, with the same designed templates: print from your browser on any printer installed on your computer (free, unlimited, nothing to install), or add the free Receipt Bridge for silent automatic printing on the events you choose — no PDF step, no print dialog, no clicks. Start with polished pre-made templates (customer receipts, kitchen tickets, delivery/pickup tickets, gift receipts, packing slips, refund slips), design image- and font-rich receipts in our visual receipt designer (try it in your browser, no account needed), or generate with AI authoring tools.

Unlike PDF/invoice plugins, ReceiptKit renders a receipt you design — line items with variations and product add-ons, totals, logo, QR codes, barcodes, huge order numbers your kitchen can read across the room — and pushes it to your printer over a fast cloud connection through a small bridge app running on your own network. Design the receipt once in the ReceiptKit editor; change it any time without touching code, and size every element independently.

Supported printers: ReceiptKit prints to Star Micronics, Epson, Rongta, Munbyn, and most ESC/POS-compatible thermal printers (via the ReceiptKit bridge). Tested end-to-end: the Star mC-Print3 (our production model) and TSP100/TSP143 series, Epson TM-T88 series, Rongta RP326, and Munbyn 80mm models; other ESC/POS printers are supported generically. Look up your model in the printer compatibility matrix — and if yours doesn’t work, there’s a form in the settings to tell us.

What you can do

  • Print any order from your browser — open an order, pick a template, click Print. The receipt is rendered in your browser and sent to whichever printer you choose in the print dialog, so it works with any printer that has a driver installed, thermal or not. Free and unlimited on every ReceiptKit plan. Each order also shows its print history.
  • Build print rules: when an order event happens (status change, refund, new order placed, or a manual button), if conditions on the order data are met, then print to the bridge, printer and template you choose.
  • Manage all your rules from one overview table — each with an enable/disable toggle and a live health indicator — and edit them in a focused pop-up.
  • See live status for every bridge and printer on your account, right on the settings screen, so you know a rule can actually reach its printer.
  • Print refund receipts automatically when an order is refunded (full or partial).
  • Route different receipts to different printers — add one rule for a counter receipt and another for a kitchen ticket on the same event.
  • Add conditions on order data: total, payment method, coupons, item SKUs/categories, country, refund amount, and more — with is / is not / greater than / less than / contains operators. Money like $12.01 is compared numerically automatically.
  • Print item variations and product add-ons (“Size: Large”, “No onions”) under each line item, plus the customer’s note — so kitchen tickets never miss a modifier.
  • Include data other plugins attach to orders — delivery/pickup dates and times, tips, gift flags — by listing the meta keys you want in settings. Only the keys you choose are sent, never an all-or-nothing dump of hidden fields.
  • Print the order’s fulfillment method (shipping vs. local pickup), status, coupon codes, fees, and a per-rate tax breakdown for VAT/GST tax-invoice receipts.
  • Works with Orderable out of the box: when the Orderable restaurant plugin is active, the service type (delivery / pickup / table), requested date and time slot, location, table number and tip are available in your templates automatically, with matching “Orderable” templates in the gallery and one-click recipes for kitchen, delivery, pickup and table tickets.
  • Open a cash drawer before/after printing, and print multiple copies.
  • Add any rule to the order screen’s Print actions menu for on-demand (re)printing.
  • Test a rule against a recent order to see exactly which conditions pass before you enable it.
  • Send a test print from any rule’s row to confirm that rule’s printer end-to-end.
  • Design branded receipts, refund slips, packing slips, and kitchen tickets in ReceiptKit.
  • Admin screens in your language: the plugin’s settings, rule editor and order screens are translated into Arabic, Danish, Dutch, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Persian, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish, Thai, Turkish and Vietnamese, and follow your WordPress language.
  • Receipts in your store’s language: the plugin tells ReceiptKit your store’s language and currency, so your ReceiptKit account can default its receipt language to match your store.

How it works

  1. Design a receipt template in your ReceiptKit dashboard (or clone a “WooCommerce Order” or “WooCommerce Refund” template from the gallery).
  2. Install this plugin, paste your ReceiptKit public key, and click Connect.
  3. Open any order and click Print in its ReceiptKit box — the receipt prints from your browser to any printer on your computer. That’s it for attended printing.
  4. Want receipts to print by themselves? Install the free ReceiptKit bridge on a computer on the same network as your printer, then add a print rule (or start from a recipe) — choose when it runs, any conditions, and what to print.
  5. Orders print automatically, silently, with no dialog.

Requirements

  • An active ReceiptKit account and public API key.
  • For browser printing: any printer installed on your computer with its manufacturer’s driver.
  • For automatic printing: the ReceiptKit bridge running next to a supported thermal printer (Star Micronics, Epson, or ESC/POS-compatible).
  • WooCommerce 8.0+ (High-Performance Order Storage supported).

External services

This plugin is a connector for ReceiptKit (https://www.receiptkit.io), the cloud receipt-printing service, and requires a ReceiptKit account. It communicates with ReceiptKit in these ways:

1. Automatic printing (bridge). When a print rule runs (or you click Test print), the plugin sends the mapped order data — line items, totals, order and customer details, your store’s name, address and phone number (from WooCommerce settings) for the receipt header, and any extra order fields you configure — to ReceiptKit’s print API at www.receiptkit.io, authenticated with your public API key, so the receipt can be rendered and delivered to your printer. Retention: by default ReceiptKit does not keep this order data after the receipt is sent to your printer. If you turn on “Design and reprint with your real orders” (offered when you connect, and in your ReceiptKit Organization settings), ReceiptKit keeps the order data of your latest 100 printed orders, none older than 30 days, so you can preview your templates with real orders, view and reprint recent receipts in your dashboard, and ReceiptKit support can see what printed; older orders are deleted automatically, and turning the setting off deletes them all right away.

2. Browser printing. Browser printing renders the receipt in your own browser; the order data never leaves it. To do that, the “Print receipt” page loads three things from your configured ReceiptKit host (www.receiptkit.io by default) over HTTPS, authenticated with your public API key where noted: (a) the template definition (your receipt design — layout, text and fields; authenticated), fetched by your server and cached locally for an hour; (b) ReceiptKit’s renderer script (/renderer/v1.0.0/receiptkit-browser-print.js), the service’s client-side component that turns a template plus order data into a printable receipt — loading it sends no order data, only the ordinary HTTP request; and (c) the font files your template uses, fetched by hash from ReceiptKit’s public font endpoint, which may redirect to ReceiptKit’s font CDN at d1uf62nizas2ue.cloudfront.net (Amazon CloudFront, operated for ReceiptKit; it serves only font files, and the request carries no order data or API key). After a receipt is printed, the plugin sends a small usage event to ReceiptKit’s API (event type, the template id, the order id, and “woocommerce” as the source) so your dashboard can show printing activity; no order contents are included.

3. Settings screen (data + live status). The settings screen loads your bridges, printers and templates from ReceiptKit’s API to populate the rule editor. It also opens a single read-only WebSocket connection (MQTT over WSS) to ReceiptKit’s live-status message broker at a3cdv9umpaq1po-ats.iot.us-east-1.amazonaws.com — an AWS IoT Core endpoint operated for ReceiptKit — authorized with your public API key, to show live bridge and printer status (online/offline, out of paper, cover open). This connection only receives status messages for your account; no order or customer data is sent over it. The MQTT client library (mqtt.min.js) is bundled with the plugin.

4. Printer support requests. If you submit the “Request printer support” form, the details you enter (printer make and model, order volume, your email, an optional note, and your store URL) are sent to ReceiptKit so we can follow up.

5. Template preview data. To set up your receipt templates so they preview the way your receipts print, the plugin sends ReceiptKit: your store name, address, phone number and logo (the site logo, WooCommerce email header image or site icon that prints best, as the image file WordPress already has); your currency, number, date and time formats; your tax rate names (for example “VAT 20%”); your first enabled shipping and payment method names; and example items (name, SKU, variation and price) from a few of your top-selling products, priced and formatted by WooCommerce. The customer on the example receipt is made up (name, email, phone and address are placeholders). What is not sent: no order, customer or personal data. When: once right after you connect, and whenever you click “Update previews from my store” on the Templates tab; never in the background. Why: ReceiptKit writes these values into your WooCommerce templates’ sample data, which previews and test prints use; real receipts always print the real order. Retention: ReceiptKit keeps the latest one with your account until it is replaced or you delete your ReceiptKit account.

6. Print rules. So your ReceiptKit dashboard can show how printing is set up, and ReceiptKit support can help when a receipt doesn’t print, the plugin sends ReceiptKit a copy of your print rules: each rule’s name, whether it is on, its event and order status, its conditions, and its printer, template, copies and cash-drawer settings. With them go the names of your Extra order fields (the template field each one becomes and its label, for example deliveryTime “Delivery time”), so the ReceiptKit designer knows your store sends them and doesn’t warn that it doesn’t. What is not sent: no order, customer or personal data, and never the values of your extra order fields. A condition on a customer field (billing email, customer note, refund reason or a custom order field) is sent without its value, marked as hidden. When: shortly after you change your rules or Extra order fields (and once after updating the plugin); unchanged rules are not sent again. Retention: ReceiptKit keeps the current rules and earlier versions with your account until you delete your ReceiptKit account. The rules in your store stay the ones that print; ReceiptKit never changes them. Each print in (1) also says what sent it (a print rule and its event, the order screen, or a test print) so your print history can show it.

7. Deactivation feedback. When you deactivate the plugin, a short optional dialog asks why. Only if you pick a reason and click “Send & deactivate”, the plugin sends ReceiptKit: the reason you picked, the note you typed (if any), your email address (only if you tick “You can email me about this”), your store URL (in WordPress’s standard User-Agent) and the plugin and WooCommerce versions. Your API key is included only if the store is connected; otherwise it is sent without one. “Skip & deactivate” sends nothing. Why: to learn what to fix, and to reply when you ask us to. Retention: ReceiptKit keeps it with your account (or, without one, with your store URL) until you delete your ReceiptKit account or ask us to remove it.

8. Diagnostics. The Settings tab has a “Send diagnostics” button for when you need help. Only when you click it, the plugin sends ReceiptKit a snapshot of how printing is set up on your store: the plugin, WooCommerce, WordPress and PHP versions; your site language and time zone; your theme and active plugins (names and versions); whether HPOS and multisite are on, and the memory limit; whether WP-Cron runs (its settings and how many scheduled tasks are late); your ReceiptKit connection (the ReceiptKit URL, whether a public or secret key is set but never the key itself, your organization name, whether ReceiptKit answered and how fast, and how many bridges, printers and templates it has); your extra order field keys and line item setting; your print rules (as in (6)); and up to 50 recent print attempts (time, order number, bridge or browser, template, rule, printer, and whether it worked or the error). What is not sent: no customer or order details; print attempts carry only the order number. “Show what will be sent” shows the exact data first, and you can copy or download it to email it instead. ReceiptKit answers with a code (for example RK-7F3A9C) to quote to support. Retention: ReceiptKit keeps each snapshot with your account until you delete your ReceiptKit account.

Every request the plugin’s server code makes to ReceiptKit carries the plugin version and the WooCommerce version (for example receiptkit-for-woocommerce/1.6.0 WooCommerce/11.1.2), alongside WordPress’s standard User-Agent (WordPress version and your store URL), so ReceiptKit support knows what your store runs.

The authenticated requests in (1), (2), (3), (5), (6) and (8) also carry your store’s language and money format: the WordPress site language (for example de_DE), the WooCommerce store currency and its symbol, the currency position, the number of price decimals, and the decimal and thousand separators. ReceiptKit stores the latest values with your account so your receipts can default to your store’s language and show prices the way your store does. These are store settings only; no order, customer or personal data is part of them. The printer support request form in (4) does not send them.

Apart from the ReceiptKit renderer script and font files described in (2), which are part of the ReceiptKit service and load only on the “Print receipt” page, no remote scripts, styles or images are loaded from any host.

ReceiptKit: terms of service, privacy policy. The live-status endpoint and the font CDN run on Amazon Web Services: AWS privacy notice, AWS service terms.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to /wp-content/plugins/receiptkit-for-woocommerce, or install it from the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate it through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to WooCommerce → ReceiptKit.
  4. Paste your public API key (starts with rk_pub_) and click Connect.
  5. Add a print rule (or start from a recipe): pick when it runs, add any conditions, and choose the bridge, printer and template. Rules save automatically.
  6. Click Test print on the rule’s row to confirm, then enable it with the toggle.
sections.faq:
How does browser printing work?

Open an order and click Print in the ReceiptKit box (or the printer icon in the orders list). The plugin renders your designed template with the order’s data right in your browser and opens the normal print dialog; choose your receipt printer and print. It needs a printer installed on that computer with its manufacturer’s driver (Star, Epson, and most others provide Windows and macOS drivers) — the driver converts the receipt for the printer, so there is nothing else to install. Set the paper size to your roll width (80 mm or 58 mm), margins to none, and turn off headers and footers. Cutting and the cash drawer are controlled by the driver’s settings. On a dedicated counter PC, Chrome’s --kiosk-printing flag prints straight to the default printer without a dialog. Browser printing is free and unlimited on every plan. For printing with no dialog and nobody at the computer — a kitchen printer, for example — install the Receipt Bridge and add a print rule.

Do I need a specific printer?

For browser printing, any printer installed on your computer works — thermal, inkjet or laser. For automatic printing through the bridge, you need a thermal printer that speaks StarPRNT, Star Raster, or ESC/POS — that covers Star Micronics, Epson, Rongta, Munbyn, and most generic ESC/POS-compatible models. Tested end-to-end: the Star mC-Print3 and TSP100/TSP143 series, the Epson TM-T88 series, the Rongta RP326, and Munbyn 80mm models. Check your exact model in the printer compatibility matrix. If your printer doesn’t work — an impact/dot-matrix model, or a brand that doesn’t follow ESC/POS — use the Request printer support form on the settings screen to tell us the make and model, and we will email you when yours is supported.

Where do I get an API key?

In your ReceiptKit dashboard under Settings → API Keys. Use your public key (rk_pub_…). It is safe to store here: it can print and read printer status, and it can’t see or change anything else in your ReceiptKit account.

How do print rules work?

Each rule is a When / If / Then automation. When an order event happens (a status change, a refund, a new order being placed, or a manual click), the rule checks if your conditions match the order’s data, and if so runs the then — one or more print actions (template + printer + optional cash drawer + copies). Add as many rules as you like; for example one for order receipts on Processing and another for a refund receipt when an order is refunded. Use the Test button on a rule to check it against your most recent order before enabling it.

Can I print refund receipts?

Yes. Add a rule whose event is Order is refunded and point it at a refund template (clone the “WooCommerce Refund” template from the gallery). It prints on both full and partial refunds, once per refund.

Can I print delivery times, tips, or other fields added by another plugin?

Yes. Many plugins (delivery-slot pickers, tip add-ons, gift options) store their data as order meta. In WooCommerce → ReceiptKit → Settings → Extra order fields, list the meta keys you want on your receipts — one per line, with an optional label after a | (for example _delivery_time | Delivery time). Each order then sends those values to your templates two ways: a repeatable metaFields list (label + value) you can drop into any template, and an individual field per key (_delivery_time becomes {{deliveryTime}}) for prominent placement — like a big pickup time at the top of a kitchen ticket. Only the keys you list are sent.

Does it work with Orderable?

Yes. Orderable orders are WooCommerce orders, so they print like any other. When Orderable is active the plugin also adds the Orderable service type (delivery, pickup or table), the requested date and time slot, the fulfilment location, and — with Orderable Pro — the table number and checkout tip to every receipt as template fields, with nothing to configure. Start from the “Orderable – Kitchen Ticket”, “Orderable – Delivery/Pickup Ticket” or “Orderable – Customer Receipt” templates in the ReceiptKit gallery, then add a rule from one of the “Orderable” recipes. Unlike Orderable’s built-in print button, receipts print automatically the moment an order is paid, on a kitchen printer that doesn’t need a screen next to it. See the Orderable setup guide.

Do item variations and add-ons print?

Yes. Each line item includes a meta field with its variations and product add-on selections (“Size: Large”, “No onions”), one per line. The WooCommerce gallery templates render it under the item name; on kitchen tickets it’s bold so modifiers never get missed.

Is High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) supported?

Yes. The plugin reads orders through WooCommerce’s standard order APIs and declares HPOS compatibility.

Will it print old orders when I activate it?

No. Each rule prints an order (or refund) once, when its event happens after the rule is configured — never retroactively.
sections.changelog:
1.8.3

  • Fixed: a print rule set to print when an order comes in now prints the complete order. Orders placed through the classic checkout page, and orders created by other plugins or the REST API, could print with no items, fees or shipping and a subtotal of 0.
  • Changed: that trigger is now called “New order is placed”, and the rule editor explains that it prints before payment is confirmed. It suits stores whose orders stay “Pending payment”, such as pay on delivery or at pickup. For card payments, print when the order status changes to Processing so only paid orders print.
  • Changed: an order whose payment fails, or that is cancelled during checkout, is no longer printed by a “New order is placed” rule.
  • Improved: an order saved before it has any items is printed once its items are added and its status changes, instead of printing an empty ticket.

1.8.2

  • Changed: the note under Connect says the next page lets you choose whether ReceiptKit keeps your recent orders so you can design and reprint with them, and “External services” says when order data is kept (only if you turn that on: your latest 100 printed orders, none older than 30 days).
  • Fixed: on the order screen, Preview now shows what the ReceiptKit box’s “For:” is set to. With a refund picked it draws that refund’s receipt (and Print… opens the refund), instead of always the order. Orders without refunds are unchanged.

1.8.1

  • Improved: your store’s logo is found in more places when you connect, so your new receipt templates start with your own logo instead of the sample one. WebP logos now work, Divi’s logo setting is read, and when no setting has a logo the plugin looks for the logo in your homepage header (for headers built with a page builder such as Elementor).
  • Improved: checking how a logo will print never uses more memory than your site has to spare; a very large image is skipped instead of risking an error.
  • Fixed: a problem while finding the logo no longer stops your products and prices from being used in the template previews.

1.8.0

  • Changed: refunds are now sent as a credit note, with the same fields as an order: the refunded items, shipping, fees and tax lines, and the refund amount as total, every amount negative (“-$12.99”) so they add up to the refund. Any order template, Line items included, now prints a refund correctly. Refunded shipping and fees, and the tax given back, now show on the receipt.
  • New: refunds include the original order’s date (orderDate), where the money went (refundedVia: the payment method, or “Manual refund” when it was paid back outside WooCommerce), and the order’s total, total refunded and remaining amount.
  • Changed: refundAmount, refundedItems and originalTotal are no longer sent. Use the refreshed “WooCommerce Refund” template from the ReceiptKit gallery.
  • New: your print rules appear on your ReceiptKit dashboard (Integrations), with the printer and template each one uses and how often it printed, and ReceiptKit support can see them when helping you. The plugin sends a copy when you change your rules, and once after updating to this version; no order or customer data is included, and a condition on a customer field is sent without its value. See “External services”.
  • New: each print tells ReceiptKit which print rule sent it (or that it came from the order screen or a test print), so a print can be traced back to its rule.
  • New: when you deactivate the plugin, an optional “Quick feedback” dialog asks why. Nothing is sent unless you pick a reason and click “Send & deactivate”; “Skip & deactivate” deactivates straight away. See “External services”.
  • New: “Send diagnostics” on the Settings tab sends ReceiptKit support a snapshot of how printing is set up on your store (versions, WP-Cron, connection, settings, print rules and recent print attempts, with no customer or order details) and gives you a code to quote in your support email. “Show what will be sent” shows the exact data, with Copy and Download for emailing it yourself. See “External services”.

1.7.0

  • New: each print now includes what was paid, one line per payment (payments: the payment method and the order total), so receipts can show the payment under the TOTAL the way tills print it.
  • New: one line per coupon (couponLines: the code and its discount) and per fee (feeLines: the fee’s name and amount), for receipts that list each one instead of a single Discount or Fees line.
  • New: for stores whose prices include tax, the discount, shipping and fees with tax (discountInclTax, shippingInclTax, feesInclTax) and pricesIncludeTax, so a “prices include tax” receipt adds up to the total, with the tax shown after it (“Incl. VAT 20%”).
  • Improved: the new fields are in your store’s template previews too. Nothing that was sent before has changed, so existing templates print exactly as before.

1.6.0

  • New: your receipt templates now preview the way your receipts print. When you connect, ReceiptKit sets up your templates in your store’s language, with your logo, currency, date format, tax names and example items from your catalog. “Update previews from my store” on the Templates tab refreshes them anytime. Preview data only; no customer or order data is included.
  • New: order totals are also sent as plain numbers (shippingAmount, taxAmount, discountAmount, feesAmount, subtotalAmount, totalAmount; tipAmount with Orderable) for template rules like “show Shipping only when it isn’t zero”. This fixes a “0,00 kr.” shipping line printing on orders without shipping in stores whose currency symbol ends in a period.
  • New: “Don’t repeat options that are already in the product name” (Settings tab, on by default). Example: “Ramen – Small” now prints without a “Size: Small” line under it, because the name already says it. Other options and add-ons still print, as in WooCommerce’s order emails. Turn it off to print every option as before.
  • New: reconnecting keeps your existing templates as they are. On ReceiptKit’s connect page you can choose to add the latest starter templates and pick which templates get your store’s preview data; “Update previews from my store” on the Templates tab lets you pick templates too. The setup card shows every template it set up, with ‹ › to browse them.
  • New: “Add the latest starter templates” on the Templates tab adds new copies of the latest Customer Receipt and Kitchen Ticket designs (and the Orderable tickets when Orderable is active) with your store’s logo, currency and example items. Your existing templates and print rules aren’t changed.
  • New: a refreshed Customer Receipt starter: your store’s address and phone in the header, one tax line per rate with your store’s own tax names, larger text, and the item total next to “qty × price” for more than one.
  • Improved: a store with no products yet previews with two example items, priced and taxed in your currency, instead of an empty receipt.
  • Improved: the Templates tab’s “Sample data” previews show each template’s own preview data, as the ReceiptKit designer does. With “An order” selected, a “View with sample data” link switches back.
  • Improved: the live printer and bridge status no longer flickers, and keeps the last known status through short connection drops.
  • Improved: the “Recommended printer” notice and the “Using a different printer?” form can be closed for good.
  • Improved: after connecting, “Choose a printer” takes you to the Printers & bridges tab, and the setup card shows the whole receipt.
  • Removed: the Sample orders tab. Template previews are now set up for you automatically.

1.5.0

  • New: preview your templates with your real orders. The new “Sample orders” tab has an on/off switch and, when on, suggests 5 varied recent orders (different shipping methods, a note, extra fields, a refund), lets you find any order by number or browse and filter recent orders, and shows each one exactly as it will be sent: as a receipt drawn with the template you pick, or as the raw data. When you change your samples later, the tab starts from the orders already on ReceiptKit. Customer details are hidden by default; notes and extra fields can be hidden too. Nothing is sent until you click “Send to ReceiptKit”, and “Delete my samples from ReceiptKit” removes them. Optional and off by default; see “External services”.
  • New: the connect step has an unchecked opt-in to set up sample orders right after connecting (it opens the Sample orders tab; nothing is sent at connect).
  • New: the Templates tab is a preview workspace. Pick a template from the list and see it large, with sample data or any of your orders (find it by number or pick a recent one). The preview is drawn in your browser; the order is not sent to ReceiptKit. From there, Print… opens the print page for that template and order, and “Use as sample” adds the order to your sample orders (nothing is sent until you click Send there).
  • New: the order screen’s ReceiptKit box has a Preview button that shows this order drawn with any of your templates in a dialog, with Print… to open the print page. It is drawn in your browser, loads only when you click it, and the order is not sent to ReceiptKit.
  • Changed: the header’s Settings button and its pop-up are replaced by a Settings tab (Connection, Extra order fields, Advanced and the setup guide). Saving returns to the tab. Before connecting, the page shows Connect and Settings tabs; “Paste it instead” opens the key field on the Settings tab.
  • New: the admin screens are translated into Arabic, Danish, Dutch, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Persian, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish, Thai, Turkish and Vietnamese (bundled with the plugin; WordPress.org language packs take precedence). They follow your WordPress language, including the rule table, rule editor, test results and live status.
  • New: requests to ReceiptKit include your store’s language and currency format (site language, currency and symbol, currency position, price decimals and separators), so your ReceiptKit account can default its receipt language to your store’s language. See “External services”.
  • Improved: counts read naturally in every language (“1 printer”, “2 printers”), and the rule table, rule editor and test results no longer show untranslated English.
  • Fixed: the order screen’s printer note now says the cash drawer stays closed unless a print rule is set to open it.
  • Improved: printing a receipt in Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Arabic, Thai and other scripts from the browser shows “Preparing fonts…” with a percentage while the fonts it needs download. If one cannot be downloaded, the page says so and offers Retry instead of printing a receipt with missing characters.
  • Improved: prices on your receipts line up exactly. Amounts in your templates no longer end with a stray space, including currencies whose symbol carries its own space (such as the Bangladeshi taka shown after the amount).

1.4.4

  • Improved: requests to ReceiptKit say which versions of this plugin and of WooCommerce sent them, so ReceiptKit support can see what your store runs. Nothing else is sent and nothing changes in your store.

1.4.3

  • New: Fields found on your recent orders. Under Extra order fields, pick the order data other plugins store (delivery dates, gift messages, pickup times) from a list read from your last 20 orders, with an example value for each, instead of typing meta keys. The list is read and shown only in your WordPress admin; a field’s value is sent only after you add it and save.
  • New: order time fields for templates: {{orderTime}} and {{orderDateTime}} in your store’s time format (plus {{refundTime}} and {{refundDateTime}} for refunds). {{orderDate}} is unchanged.
  • New: tax-inclusive prices for stores that show prices with tax: {{items.priceInclTax}}, {{items.totalInclTax}} and {{subtotalInclTax}}, so line items add up to the order total.
  • Improved: sample prints use a sample phone number and addresses shaped like real WooCommerce orders.
  • Fixed: the Orderable print-rule presets named templates that don’t exist; they now point to the Delivery Driver Ticket, Packing Slip and Order Confirmation templates.

1.4.2

  • Improved: the print page shows where a receipt is going. A Send to control sits right beside Print, with a line explaining what will happen, and your choice is remembered for this browser and as the store default, so you no longer re-pick the printer on every visit.
  • Improved: Preview / Print and the Templates tab thumbnails render templates that were designed for other data (a POS receipt, a label) with the template’s own sample values instead of literal placeholders. Applies to sample prints only; real order prints are unchanged.
  • Fixed: sample prints showed a “-$0.00” discount line that real orders hide.
  • Changed: the “Orderable templates” gallery button on the Templates tab is gone; the connect notice links to the WooCommerce gallery filter instead.
  • Note: ReceiptKit’s font update (45 families, real bold weights) reaches browser printing through the hosted renderer, no plugin update needed. If a store’s receipts still print with the old fonts, hard-refresh the print page once.

1.4.1

  • New: if Orderable is active when you click Connect with ReceiptKit, the Orderable kitchen ticket, driver ticket, packing slip, and order confirmation templates are added to your account along with the WooCommerce starters. The Templates tab also gets an “Orderable templates” gallery button.

1.4.0

  • New: Connect with ReceiptKit. One button links the store: sign in (or create a free account), confirm, and you’re back in WordPress connected — no API key to copy. ReceiptKit creates a key just for this store and adds a Customer Receipt and a Kitchen Ticket template.
  • New: on a first connect with no print rules yet, an “Order receipt” rule is created for you (switched off) pointing at the new Customer Receipt template — use Preview / Print to check it, then switch it on.
  • New: Settings → Connection has Switch to a different account and Disconnect. Disconnecting keeps your print rules. Pasting a key manually still works under “Change the key manually”.
  • Changed: the manual-key modal no longer opens automatically on first run when one-click connect is available.
  • Changed: each print rule has one Preview / Print button. It opens the sample receipt page with the rule’s template and printer already selected (“This computer” when the rule has no printer) — preview it, change the choices, or print it from there. Replaces the separate “Test print” and “Print in browser” buttons.
  • Changed: the sample receipt page can print to a bridge printer as well as the browser’s print dialog.
  • New: the settings page is now tabbed: Print rules, Templates, and Printers & bridges. The Templates tab shows every template on your account rendered with sample order data, with Preview / Print, Edit in ReceiptKit, and New from the gallery (opens the gallery filtered to the WooCommerce starters). The Printers & bridges tab shows “This computer” plus each bridge and its printers with live status, or how to get the bridge if you have none.

1.3.0

  • New: Print any receipt to any printer from the order screen. The ReceiptKit box is now a simple chooser — pick a receipt and a printer, click Print. “This computer” prints through your browser’s print dialog; a named printer prints through your Receipt Bridge in place, with the result shown right there and no page reload. Your last choice becomes the default.
  • New: a Receipt column in the orders list: one click prints the default receipt to the default printer; the caret opens the chooser. Shows by default on both order storage modes.
  • Changed: the “Print receipt” preview page has the same Receipt and Printer choices, prefilled from where you opened it, and its Print button sends to the selected printer.
  • Changed: the print history names the printer for bridge prints.

1.2.3

  • New: when a store prints 10 or more receipts from the browser in a week and has no Receipt Bridge yet, the settings page suggests installing the free bridge for automatic printing (with a “Remind me later” that hides it for two weeks). The counts come from ReceiptKit; browser prints are never metered.

1.2.2

  • Improved: the ReceiptKit box on the order screen now sits at the top of the sidebar, next to Order actions, instead of below the order notes.

1.2.1

  • Fix: the “Print receipt” page returned “Sorry, you are not allowed to access this page” in 1.2.0 (hidden admin page registration). Browser printing now works from the order screen, the orders list, and the settings sample button.

1.2.0

  • New: Browser printing. Print any order (or refund) from the order screen with your designed template, through your browser’s print dialog, to any printer installed on your computer — no bridge required. Free and unlimited. Every order gets a ReceiptKit box with template choice, Preview and Print buttons, and a print history (bridge and browser prints, with who printed and whether it succeeded); the orders list gets a print icon; each rule row gets a “Print in browser” sample print.
  • New: template definitions are cached locally for an hour so browser prints keep working during a brief ReceiptKit outage.
  • Changed: the setup guide now gets you to a first browser print before suggesting the Receipt Bridge; the bridge is optional and only needed for silent automatic printing.
  • Docs: “External services” documents the hosted renderer script, template and font loads, and the usage event used by browser printing.

1.1.0

  • New: Orderable integration. When the Orderable restaurant plugin is active, the service type, delivery/pickup date and time slot, location, table number and tip are added to every receipt as template fields automatically ({{serviceType}}, {{serviceDateTime}}, {{locationName}}, {{tableNumber}}, {{tip}}), the rule builder gains an “Orderable” condition group, and one-click recipes for kitchen, delivery, pickup, table and customer-receipt rules appear. Pairs with the new “Orderable” templates in the ReceiptKit gallery.

1.0.8

  • Fixed: the WordPress.org listing banner now says “Auto-print receipts” instead of “Auto-print orders”.

1.0.7

  • Improved: links from the plugin to receiptkit.io are now tagged so we can see which customers arrived through the plugin.

1.0.6

  • Improved: the rules table now shows a clear “Off” status for switched-off rules instead of the printer-health chip, so a disabled rule can’t read as “Ready”.
  • Improved: the rule editor notes that newly added blank rules start switched off (rules created from a recipe start on).
  • Fixed: the status chip now refreshes immediately when a rule is toggled on or off.

1.0.5

  • Documentation: “External services” is now its own top-level readme section and fully documents the live-status WebSocket connection (the AWS IoT Core endpoint used by the settings screen) alongside the print API and the printer-request form, with terms and privacy links for both ReceiptKit and AWS.
  • Copy: settings-screen text updated to say “receipt printer” rather than “Star printer” — reflecting all supported brands.

1.0.4

  • Clarified in code that the AWS IoT hostname in the live-status module is a WebSocket data endpoint (documented under “External services”) — no remote scripts, styles, or images are loaded; the MQTT client library is bundled with the plugin.

1.0.3

  • Tested up to WordPress 7.1 (verified on a live 7.1 + WooCommerce 10.9 store).

1.0.2

  • Docs: printer compatibility notes now name the tested Epson TM-T88 series, Rongta RP326, and Munbyn 80mm models, and link to the full model-by-model compatibility matrix.

1.0.1

  • Improved: the rule editor now refreshes your bridges, printers and templates from ReceiptKit every time it opens, so renames made in the dashboard show up immediately.
  • Changed: new rules default to appearing in the order screen’s “Print” actions menu (uncheck the option in the rule editor to opt out).

1.0.0

  • First stable release.
  • New: line items now include their variations and product add-ons (meta), so kitchen tickets can print every modifier.
  • New: “Extra order fields” setting — list order meta keys (delivery/pickup times, tips, gift flags from other plugins) to include on receipts, selectively. Each key is sent as a labeled metaFields row and as its own template field (e.g. _delivery_time → deliveryTime).
  • New: order payload now includes fulfillment method (shippingMethod), order status, coupon codes, fees, and a per-rate tax breakdown (taxLines) for VAT/GST tax-invoice templates.
  • New: gallery starter templates for a Delivery/Pickup ticket, a Gift Receipt (prices hidden), and a Tax Invoice (VAT/ABN header with per-rate tax breakdown); the Customer Receipt now prints item options and the customer’s note.

0.2.2

  • Maintenance release: build/packaging refresh. No functional changes.

0.2.1

  • New: rules that point at a template which has since been archived or deleted in ReceiptKit now show a clear “Template unavailable” warning instead of silently blanking the selection, and the saved template is preserved so you can review it before choosing a current one.

0.2.0

  • New: rule-based printing (When / If / Then). Each rule prints to one destination — a bridge, printer and template you choose.
  • New: print rules overview table with a per-rule enable/disable toggle and a live health indicator, plus a modal editor.
  • New: bridge-first rule editor — pick a bridge (auto-selected when you have only one), see its live status, then pick a printer on it and a template.
  • New: live device status — a Devices panel shows every bridge and printer on your account and whether each is online, out of paper, etc.
  • New: automatic refund receipts (full and partial refunds) via a “WooCommerce Refund” template.
  • New: one-click recipes, per-field hints, autosave (no page reloads), and a “Test against a recent order” check.
  • New: add any rule to the order screen’s Print actions menu.
  • Conditions compare money strings numerically and never error on empty/invalid values; a print failure can never interrupt an order.

0.1.0

  • Initial release: auto-print WooCommerce orders to a Star Micronics printer via ReceiptKit, with printer/template selection, cash-drawer control, and a test print.

short_description: Print designed receipts for online orders on thermal printers. Free browser printing on any printer; silent automatic printing with the bridge.
description:
Print real receipts for your online orders — not invoices, receipts. Two ways to print, with the same designed templates: print from your browser on any printer installed on your computer (free, unlimited, nothing to install), or add the free Receipt Bridge for silent automatic printing on the events you choose — no PDF step, no print dialog, no clicks. Start with polished pre-made templates (customer receipts, kitchen tickets, delivery/pickup tickets, gift receipts, packing slips, refund slips), design image- and font-rich receipts in our visual receipt designer (try it in your browser, no account needed), or generate with AI authoring tools.

Unlike PDF/invoice plugins, ReceiptKit renders a receipt you design — line items with variations and product add-ons, totals, logo, QR codes, barcodes, huge order numbers your kitchen can read across the room — and pushes it to your printer over a fast cloud connection through a small bridge app running on your own network. Design the receipt once in the ReceiptKit editor; change it any time without touching code, and size every element independently.

Supported printers: ReceiptKit prints to Star Micronics, Epson, Rongta, Munbyn, and most ESC/POS-compatible thermal printers (via the ReceiptKit bridge). Tested end-to-end: the Star mC-Print3 (our production model) and TSP100/TSP143 series, Epson TM-T88 series, Rongta RP326, and Munbyn 80mm models; other ESC/POS printers are supported generically. Look up your model in the printer compatibility matrix — and if yours doesn’t work, there’s a form in the settings to tell us.

What you can do

  • Print any order from your browser — open an order, pick a template, click Print. The receipt is rendered in your browser and sent to whichever printer you choose in the print dialog, so it works with any printer that has a driver installed, thermal or not. Free and unlimited on every ReceiptKit plan. Each order also shows its print history.
  • Build print rules: when an order event happens (status change, refund, new order placed, or a manual button), if conditions on the order data are met, then print to the bridge, printer and template you choose.
  • Manage all your rules from one overview table — each with an enable/disable toggle and a live health indicator — and edit them in a focused pop-up.
  • See live status for every bridge and printer on your account, right on the settings screen, so you know a rule can actually reach its printer.
  • Print refund receipts automatically when an order is refunded (full or partial).
  • Route different receipts to different printers — add one rule for a counter receipt and another for a kitchen ticket on the same event.
  • Add conditions on order data: total, payment method, coupons, item SKUs/categories, country, refund amount, and more — with is / is not / greater than / less than / contains operators. Money like $12.01 is compared numerically automatically.
  • Print item variations and product add-ons (“Size: Large”, “No onions”) under each line item, plus the customer’s note — so kitchen tickets never miss a modifier.
  • Include data other plugins attach to orders — delivery/pickup dates and times, tips, gift flags — by listing the meta keys you want in settings. Only the keys you choose are sent, never an all-or-nothing dump of hidden fields.
  • Print the order’s fulfillment method (shipping vs. local pickup), status, coupon codes, fees, and a per-rate tax breakdown for VAT/GST tax-invoice receipts.
  • Works with Orderable out of the box: when the Orderable restaurant plugin is active, the service type (delivery / pickup / table), requested date and time slot, location, table number and tip are available in your templates automatically, with matching “Orderable” templates in the gallery and one-click recipes for kitchen, delivery, pickup and table tickets.
  • Open a cash drawer before/after printing, and print multiple copies.
  • Add any rule to the order screen’s Print actions menu for on-demand (re)printing.
  • Test a rule against a recent order to see exactly which conditions pass before you enable it.
  • Send a test print from any rule’s row to confirm that rule’s printer end-to-end.
  • Design branded receipts, refund slips, packing slips, and kitchen tickets in ReceiptKit.
  • Admin screens in your language: the plugin’s settings, rule editor and order screens are translated into Arabic, Danish, Dutch, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Persian, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish, Thai, Turkish and Vietnamese, and follow your WordPress language.
  • Receipts in your store’s language: the plugin tells ReceiptKit your store’s language and currency, so your ReceiptKit account can default its receipt language to match your store.

How it works

  1. Design a receipt template in your ReceiptKit dashboard (or clone a “WooCommerce Order” or “WooCommerce Refund” template from the gallery).
  2. Install this plugin, paste your ReceiptKit public key, and click Connect.
  3. Open any order and click Print in its ReceiptKit box — the receipt prints from your browser to any printer on your computer. That’s it for attended printing.
  4. Want receipts to print by themselves? Install the free ReceiptKit bridge on a computer on the same network as your printer, then add a print rule (or start from a recipe) — choose when it runs, any conditions, and what to print.
  5. Orders print automatically, silently, with no dialog.

Requirements

  • An active ReceiptKit account and public API key.
  • For browser printing: any printer installed on your computer with its manufacturer’s driver.
  • For automatic printing: the ReceiptKit bridge running next to a supported thermal printer (Star Micronics, Epson, or ESC/POS-compatible).
  • WooCommerce 8.0+ (High-Performance Order Storage supported).

External services

This plugin is a connector for ReceiptKit (https://www.receiptkit.io), the cloud receipt-printing service, and requires a ReceiptKit account. It communicates with ReceiptKit in these ways:

1. Automatic printing (bridge). When a print rule runs (or you click Test print), the plugin sends the mapped order data — line items, totals, order and customer details, your store’s name, address and phone number (from WooCommerce settings) for the receipt header, and any extra order fields you configure — to ReceiptKit’s print API at www.receiptkit.io, authenticated with your public API key, so the receipt can be rendered and delivered to your printer. Retention: by default ReceiptKit does not keep this order data after the receipt is sent to your printer. If you turn on “Design and reprint with your real orders” (offered when you connect, and in your ReceiptKit Organization settings), ReceiptKit keeps the order data of your latest 100 printed orders, none older than 30 days, so you can preview your templates with real orders, view and reprint recent receipts in your dashboard, and ReceiptKit support can see what printed; older orders are deleted automatically, and turning the setting off deletes them all right away.

2. Browser printing. Browser printing renders the receipt in your own browser; the order data never leaves it. To do that, the “Print receipt” page loads three things from your configured ReceiptKit host (www.receiptkit.io by default) over HTTPS, authenticated with your public API key where noted: (a) the template definition (your receipt design — layout, text and fields; authenticated), fetched by your server and cached locally for an hour; (b) ReceiptKit’s renderer script (/renderer/v1.0.0/receiptkit-browser-print.js), the service’s client-side component that turns a template plus order data into a printable receipt — loading it sends no order data, only the ordinary HTTP request; and (c) the font files your template uses, fetched by hash from ReceiptKit’s public font endpoint, which may redirect to ReceiptKit’s font CDN at d1uf62nizas2ue.cloudfront.net (Amazon CloudFront, operated for ReceiptKit; it serves only font files, and the request carries no order data or API key). After a receipt is printed, the plugin sends a small usage event to ReceiptKit’s API (event type, the template id, the order id, and “woocommerce” as the source) so your dashboard can show printing activity; no order contents are included.

3. Settings screen (data + live status). The settings screen loads your bridges, printers and templates from ReceiptKit’s API to populate the rule editor. It also opens a single read-only WebSocket connection (MQTT over WSS) to ReceiptKit’s live-status message broker at a3cdv9umpaq1po-ats.iot.us-east-1.amazonaws.com — an AWS IoT Core endpoint operated for ReceiptKit — authorized with your public API key, to show live bridge and printer status (online/offline, out of paper, cover open). This connection only receives status messages for your account; no order or customer data is sent over it. The MQTT client library (mqtt.min.js) is bundled with the plugin.

4. Printer support requests. If you submit the “Request printer support” form, the details you enter (printer make and model, order volume, your email, an optional note, and your store URL) are sent to ReceiptKit so we can follow up.

5. Template preview data. To set up your receipt templates so they preview the way your receipts print, the plugin sends ReceiptKit: your store name, address, phone number and logo (the site logo, WooCommerce email header image or site icon that prints best, as the image file WordPress already has); your currency, number, date and time formats; your tax rate names (for example “VAT 20%”); your first enabled shipping and payment method names; and example items (name, SKU, variation and price) from a few of your top-selling products, priced and formatted by WooCommerce. The customer on the example receipt is made up (name, email, phone and address are placeholders). What is not sent: no order, customer or personal data. When: once right after you connect, and whenever you click “Update previews from my store” on the Templates tab; never in the background. Why: ReceiptKit writes these values into your WooCommerce templates’ sample data, which previews and test prints use; real receipts always print the real order. Retention: ReceiptKit keeps the latest one with your account until it is replaced or you delete your ReceiptKit account.

6. Print rules. So your ReceiptKit dashboard can show how printing is set up, and ReceiptKit support can help when a receipt doesn’t print, the plugin sends ReceiptKit a copy of your print rules: each rule’s name, whether it is on, its event and order status, its conditions, and its printer, template, copies and cash-drawer settings. With them go the names of your Extra order fields (the template field each one becomes and its label, for example deliveryTime “Delivery time”), so the ReceiptKit designer knows your store sends them and doesn’t warn that it doesn’t. What is not sent: no order, customer or personal data, and never the values of your extra order fields. A condition on a customer field (billing email, customer note, refund reason or a custom order field) is sent without its value, marked as hidden. When: shortly after you change your rules or Extra order fields (and once after updating the plugin); unchanged rules are not sent again. Retention: ReceiptKit keeps the current rules and earlier versions with your account until you delete your ReceiptKit account. The rules in your store stay the ones that print; ReceiptKit never changes them. Each print in (1) also says what sent it (a print rule and its event, the order screen, or a test print) so your print history can show it.

7. Deactivation feedback. When you deactivate the plugin, a short optional dialog asks why. Only if you pick a reason and click “Send & deactivate”, the plugin sends ReceiptKit: the reason you picked, the note you typed (if any), your email address (only if you tick “You can email me about this”), your store URL (in WordPress’s standard User-Agent) and the plugin and WooCommerce versions. Your API key is included only if the store is connected; otherwise it is sent without one. “Skip & deactivate” sends nothing. Why: to learn what to fix, and to reply when you ask us to. Retention: ReceiptKit keeps it with your account (or, without one, with your store URL) until you delete your ReceiptKit account or ask us to remove it.

8. Diagnostics. The Settings tab has a “Send diagnostics” button for when you need help. Only when you click it, the plugin sends ReceiptKit a snapshot of how printing is set up on your store: the plugin, WooCommerce, WordPress and PHP versions; your site language and time zone; your theme and active plugins (names and versions); whether HPOS and multisite are on, and the memory limit; whether WP-Cron runs (its settings and how many scheduled tasks are late); your ReceiptKit connection (the ReceiptKit URL, whether a public or secret key is set but never the key itself, your organization name, whether ReceiptKit answered and how fast, and how many bridges, printers and templates it has); your extra order field keys and line item setting; your print rules (as in (6)); and up to 50 recent print attempts (time, order number, bridge or browser, template, rule, printer, and whether it worked or the error). What is not sent: no customer or order details; print attempts carry only the order number. “Show what will be sent” shows the exact data first, and you can copy or download it to email it instead. ReceiptKit answers with a code (for example RK-7F3A9C) to quote to support. Retention: ReceiptKit keeps each snapshot with your account until you delete your ReceiptKit account.

Every request the plugin’s server code makes to ReceiptKit carries the plugin version and the WooCommerce version (for example receiptkit-for-woocommerce/1.6.0 WooCommerce/11.1.2), alongside WordPress’s standard User-Agent (WordPress version and your store URL), so ReceiptKit support knows what your store runs.

The authenticated requests in (1), (2), (3), (5), (6) and (8) also carry your store’s language and money format: the WordPress site language (for example de_DE), the WooCommerce store currency and its symbol, the currency position, the number of price decimals, and the decimal and thousand separators. ReceiptKit stores the latest values with your account so your receipts can default to your store’s language and show prices the way your store does. These are store settings only; no order, customer or personal data is part of them. The printer support request form in (4) does not send them.

Apart from the ReceiptKit renderer script and font files described in (2), which are part of the ReceiptKit service and load only on the “Print receipt” page, no remote scripts, styles or images are loaded from any host.

ReceiptKit: terms of service, privacy policy. The live-status endpoint and the font CDN run on Amazon Web Services: AWS privacy notice, AWS service terms.
